content: Hairy cell leukemia accounts for approximately 2% of all leukemia cases in the United States. The prevalence is estimated to be about 2 cases per 1,000,000 individuals in the U.S. population. The incidence of hairy cell leukemia increases with advancing age, with the median age at diagnosis being 58 years. Males are significantly more affected by hairy cell leukemia compared to females, with a male-to-female ratio of approximately 4:1. Hairy cell leukemia is considered one of the least common subtypes of leukemia in the United States. Over the past 30 years, the incidence rate of this disease has remained relatively stable. The disease predominantly affects individuals of Caucasian descent. In contrast, individuals of Asian and African American descent are less likely to develop hairy cell leukemia.
